transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I've been having some trouble staying seated. Like, when I'm supposed to just stay put. 

It happens during client interviews for work, or when I'm tutoring... even at my book club. I just keep getting up. And, well, people are starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When you get up, do you feel an inner restlessness that makes it hard to stay still?

I guess so. I just... I don't really stop moving. Even on days when I don't have field work, I'm still just going. 

I'll move from unpacking boxes to, um, reorganizing case files... or running errands. It's almost like I'm chasing a lead, even when there isn't one. I just have a hard time being off duty, I suppose.
Did this restlessness start after you began taking a medication or after a dose change?
No... I don't think so. I haven't started taking anything new. So... no, it's not that.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or activated for days at a time?

Um... no. Not really. 

It's not like it comes in phases or anything like that. I'm just... kind of always like this.
Were you this fidgety and unable to stay seated when you were a child?

I suppose. Um... my mother still jokes about it, actually. She says I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through. And... I know my old grade-school report cards always said I was bright, but... that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. So... yeah. Always been like that, I guess.
Before you get up, do you usually have an unwanted thought or fear that feels like it has to be relieved by standing or moving?
No. Um... nothing like that. I just... get up. There's no specific thought or fear making me do it.

Prior alternatives F41.1, F42.8, and F63.9 are less consistent and removed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern of hyperactivity/restlessness with inability to remain seated across multiple settings, beginning in childhood and causing noticeable interpersonal/occupational impairment. Symptoms are chronic rather than episodic, with no evidence for medication-induced akathisia, manic activation, or compulsive behavior driven by intrusive thoughts. This is most consistent with disturbance of activity and attention (ADHD/hyperkinetic disorder), predominantly reflected here by hyperactivity/impulsivity.
